name: IN-09
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans about 15 points Republican and Houchin is the incumbent
Houchin holds a roughly 10-to-1 financial advantage ($1.27M to $53K on hand)
Prediction markets price Houchin's re-election near 97 percent
No public polls or expert ratings flag the race as competitive
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Houchin's incumbency, and her overwhelming fundraising edge over Brad Meyer all point the same direction, and markets price her re-election at near-certain. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting a contest, there is no evidence supporting a move toward the Democrat.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Houchin or a strong national Democratic wave could narrow the margin, though an upset would still require an unusual shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 9th District leans heavily Republican, and incumbent Erin Houchin is seeking re-election against Democrat Brad Meyer and Libertarian Tonya Hudson. The district's partisan lean of roughly fifteen points Republican, combined with Houchin's incumbency, gives the Republican a strong structural advantage in this southern Indiana seat.

Financial figures underscore the imbalance: Houchin has raised about $2.2 million and holds $1.3 million on hand, while Meyer has raised roughly $195,000 with about $53,000 available. Prediction markets give Houchin roughly a 97 percent chance of winning. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's underlying partisan lean, which points clearly toward the incumbent. A significant national Democratic wave or an unexpected campaign development would be needed to make this competitive; as it stands, Houchin is strongly favored to return to Congress.
